CRM notes (shorthand):
- Account summary: Elmwood Orbit builds product help & knowledge center for mid-market SaaS customers. Heavy embeddings + rerank for search; chat assistant for tier-1 support.
- POC path: started on Hosted API to validate output quality and integration. After Hosted POC, moved to small Dedicated pilot to measure tail latency and cost predictability.
- Technical targets: target p95 latency <120ms for chat flows, sustained throughput ~250 reqs/sec with occasional bursts to 600 reqs/sec. Embedding pipeline 40k/day.
- Pricing ask: want committed capacity pricing with predictable monthly invoice. Preferences: 12-mo ramp (month1 25% commit, M3 50%, M6 75%), burst buffer for seasonal spikes, clear overage rate (prefer not >1.5x committed unit price).
- POC results (summary): dedicated pilot reduced per-token cost ~42% vs hosted when using continuous batching + prefix cache; however 4-bit quantization introduced a small quality regression (~1% on rubric) — engineering prefers mixed precision (8-bit) for critical flows.
- Security/compliance: must pass SOC2 checklist; SSO/SAML & KMS integration required; data residency for EU subset customers later this year. Legal asked for subprocessors list and incident response SLA.
- Budget: procurement indicated target ARR band $200k-$450k; prefer opex monthly billing but will consider committed annual with discount.
- Quote negotiation notes: AE Maya proposed three commit tiers (Small 2x A100 equiv, Medium 4x, Large 8x) + 30% burst headroom. Finance asked for explicit formula for overage charges and pro-rated ramp credits. Devon to provide cost model spreadsheet.
- Customer quotes: "We need a predictable monthly line-item we can commit to — unpredictable per-token bills are a blocker for our CFO."
- Risk: engineering wants to re-run synthetic load test with customer's real query distribution to validate p95 SLAs; schedule pending.
- Next steps: update SOW with revised ramp schedule and overage cap; legal to receive redline-ready doc by 2026-03-20.
